explanation: The head is widely considered the most sacred part of the body in Indonesia, believed by many to be where the spirit resides, so touching someone else's head — including a child's — is seen as disrespectful. This view is reinforced by Islamic tradition in the country's Muslim-majority areas. Even a well-meaning pat can cause real offense.
local_tip: Avoid touching anyone's head, even affectionately with children; use a smile, a nod, or a light touch on the shoulder instead.

also_check.note: The head is considered the body's highest and most sacred point; touching it is a major faux pas.
Patting a child's head is sometimes tolerated, but touching an adult's head is seen as condescending.
Patting a child's head is often read as affectionate or encouraging.
